Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Rapid-onset upper-lip swelling beginning ~30 min after prawn soup  
• Progressive enlargement with throat tightness, dyspnoea, dizziness  
• History of atopy: peanut allergy, asthma, prior food-related swelling episode  

Working diagnosis  
• IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to shellfish (prawn) – high likelihood based on timing, rapid progression, airway involvement, and atopic history.

Considerations  
• Isolated allergic angioedema without systemic anaphylaxis – medium likelihood but respiratory symptoms make this less likely.  
• Hereditary angioedema – low-medium likelihood; food trigger and atopy argue against.

Management actions already taken  
• Clinician initiated emergency response: advised immediate ambulance call (suspected anaphylaxis).  
• Advised prompt oral antihistamine while awaiting paramedics.  

Post-hospital planning (to be arranged after acute episode)  
• Prescribe epinephrine auto-injector and educate on use.  
• Arrange allergy referral for shellfish testing and action plan.  
• Review need for asthma control optimization.  
• Discuss carrying antihistamines and medical alert identification.

  • Education to avoid known allergens (peanut, shellfish) and to carry epinephrine once prescribed.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to shellfish (prawn) – High likelihood. Justified by rapid onset after exposure, progressive lip/throat swelling, dyspnoea, dizziness, and atopic history.  
2. Isolated allergic angioedema to shellfish – Medium likelihood. Supports lip swelling but systemic features suggest broader anaphylaxis.  
3. Hereditary angioedema – Low-Medium likelihood. Recurrent swelling possible, but clear allergen trigger and atopy make this less probable.
